dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: Good morning to you. Did you wake up early?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، اسْتَيْقَظْتُ مُبَكِّرًا، لَكِنِّي مَا زِلْتُ نَعْسَان.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, istayqadhtu mubakkiran, lakinnee maa zaltu na3saan.
dialogue.english: Yes, I woke up early, but I'm still sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Here you are, this is your coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.transliteration: shukran. ghasaltu wajhee wa nadhdhaftu asnaanee.
dialogue.english: Thanks. I washed my face and brushed my teeth.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: وَأَنَا لَبِسْتُ مَلَابِسِي. سَأَخْرُجُ إِلَى الْعَمَل.
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa labistu malaabisee. sa2akhruju ilaa al-3amal.
dialogue.english: And I got dressed. I'll leave for work.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: الصَّبَاحُ الْبَاكِرُ بَارِدٌ جِدًّا، خُذْ مِعْطَفَكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: as-sabaa7u al-baakiru baaridun jiddan, khudh mi3tafaka.
dialogue.english: Early morning is very cold, take your coat.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Fine. I'm afraid I'll miss the bus.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: Go quickly!

pair.english: When did you leave the house?

lessons.culture: A morning greeting is answered with a richer one: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر is met by صَبَاحُ النُّور. Hours are said with the ordinal number, so السَّاعَةُ السَّابِعَة is literally 'the seventh hour'.

exercises.tip: The reply gives back a brighter word: 'morning of light'.

phrases.arabic: يَجِبُ أَنْ أُنْهِيَ هَذِهِ الْمُهِمَّةَ قَبْلَ الظُّهْر
phrases.transliteration: yajibu an unhiya haadhihi al-muhimmata qabla adh-dhuhr

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا سَارَة. وَصَلْتُ إِلَى الْعَمَل مُبَكِّرًا.
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7u al-khayr yaa Saara. wasaltu ilaa al-3amal mubakkiran.
dialogue.english: Good morning, Sara. I arrived at work early.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: أَهْلًا يَا طَارِق. عِنْدِي اجْتِمَاعٌ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْعَاشِرَة.
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan yaa Taariq. 3indee ijtimaa3un fee as-saa3ati al-3aashira.
dialogue.english: Hello, Tariq. I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: And I have a lot of work now.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: لَا جَدِيدَ، لَكِنْ يَجِبُ أَنْ أُنْهِيَ هَذِهِ الْمُهِمَّةَ قَبْلَ الظُّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: laa jadeed, lakin yajibu an unhiya haadhihi al-muhimmata qabla adh-dhuhr.
dialogue.english: Nothing new, but I have to finish this task before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: I'm looking for my pen. Have you seen it?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: No, I haven't seen it.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: وَجَدْتُهُ. أَنَا جَائِعَةٌ، أُرِيدُ أَنْ آكُلَ شَيْئًا.
dialogue.transliteration: wajadtuhu. anaa jaa2i3a, ureedu an aakula shay2an.
dialogue.english: I found it. I'm hungry, I want to eat something.

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.english: Where do you have lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: فِي الْمَطْعَمِ الْقَرِيب. هَلْ تَأْتِي مَعِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: fee al-mat3ami al-qareeb. hal ta2tee ma3ee?
dialogue.english: At the nearby restaurant. Will you come with me?

dialogue.speaker: Tariq
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، لَكِنْ بَعْدَ أَنْ آخُذَ اسْتِرَاحَة.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, lakin ba3da an aakhudha istiraa7a.
dialogue.english: Yes, but after I take a break.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: خُذْ وَقْتَكَ. سَأَتَّصِلُ بِكَ بَعْدَ الظُّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: khudh waqtaka. sa2attasilu bika ba3da adh-dhuhr.
dialogue.english: Take your time. I'll call you in the afternoon.

response.english: I'll call you in the afternoon.

lessons.culture: The working day often starts early, and الْغَدَاء, lunch, is the main meal, usually eaten after الظُّهْر, the midday time. Asking مَا أَخْبَارُ الْيَوْم؟ is a friendly way to start talking with a colleague.

dialogue.speaker: Hassan

lessons.culture: Evening greetings mirror the morning ones: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر is answered with مَسَاءُ النُّور. At night people say تُصْبِحُ عَلَى خَيْر, literally 'may you wake up well', and the reply wishes the same goodness back.

lessons.culture: In much of the Arab world the working week runs from Sunday to Thursday, with Friday as the day of congregational prayer and rest and Saturday as the second weekend day. Some countries now use a Saturday and Sunday weekend, so it is worth asking.

lessons.culture: Arabic calligraphy is one of the most loved arts in the Muslim world, because it grew from the care taken to write the Qur'an beautifully. Learners start with simple scripts such as naskh and ruq'a, then move to grand ones such as thuluth and diwani. Many people also enjoy a quiet hobby like reading, cooking for the family or gardening in their free time.

dialogue.english: Yes, but I'm tired now. I need water.

pair.english: Shall we walk together after the prayer?

lessons.culture: Football is the most popular sport across the Arab world, and match nights fill cafes and homes with fans. Archery and horse riding hold a special place in Islamic tradition, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, encouraged them. Many people also walk or run in the cool of the morning, and keep sport separate for men and women in public clubs.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I run every morning.'
Translate: 'I ride my bicycle in the park.'
Which word means 'match, game'?
exercises.tip: مُبَارَاة is a match between two teams.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Archery is my favourite sport'?
Put these words in order: 'الْقَدَمِ / أَلْعَبُ / أَصْدِقَائِي / كُرَةَ / مَعَ'.
exercises.tip: كُرَةُ الْقَدَم is 'football', literally 'ball of the foot'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'مُفِيدَةٌ / الرِّيَاضَةُ / لِلصِّحَّة'.
Complete: 'أَرْفَعُ الْأَثْقَالَ فِي _____ الرِّيَاضِيّ.' (I lift weights at the gym.)
Complete: 'أَنَا مُتْعَبٌ، أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى _____.' (I'm tired, I need water.)
A friend asks: 'هَلْ تُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَة؟'. Say yes, you play football.
A friend asks: 'هَلْ نَمْشِي مَعًا بَعْدَ الصَّلَاة؟'. Say 'With pleasure.'
exercises.tip: بِكُلِّ سُرُور is a warm way to say yes.

challenge.title: My day and my week
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha between two people. They greet each other in the morning, say the time, describe what they did before work, plan lunch and a meeting, meet again in the evening, talk about dinner, say what day it is and plan the weekend, and end with good night.
required_elements: a morning greeting and its reply
the time of day given as an hour
two or three things done in the morning
a plan for lunch or a meeting at a given hour
an evening greeting and plans for the evening
days of the week and a weekend plan

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا آدَم. كَمِ السَّاعَةُ الْآن؟
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7u al-khayr yaa Aadam. kami as-saa3atu al-aan?
dialogue.english: Good morning, Adam. What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: صَبَاحُ النُّور. السَّاعَةُ السَّابِعَة، وَمَا زِلْتُ نَعْسَان.
dialogue.transliteration: sabaa7u an-noor. as-saa3atu as-saabi3a, wa maa zaltu na3saan.
dialogue.english: Good morning. It's seven o'clock, and I'm still sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: اِسْتَيْقَظْتُ مُبَكِّرًا وَنَظَّفْتُ أَسْنَانِي وَخَرَجْتُ إِلَى الْعَمَل.
dialogue.transliteration: istayqadhtu mubakkiran wa nadhdhaftu asnaanee wa kharajtu ilaa al-3amal.
dialogue.english: I woke up early, brushed my teeth and left for work.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.english: Where do you have lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: فِي الْمَطْعَمِ الْقَرِيب. سَأَتَّصِلُ بِكِ بَعْدَ الظُّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: fee al-mat3ami al-qareeb. sa2attasilu biki ba3da adh-dhuhr.
dialogue.english: At the nearby restaurant. I'll call you in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر. عُدْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْت وَتَعِبْتُ كَثِيرًا الْيَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: masaa2u al-khayr. 3udtu ilaa al-bayt wa ta3ibtu katheeran al-yawm.
dialogue.english: Good evening. I came back home and got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: مَسَاءُ النُّور. مَاذَا سَنَأْكُلُ عَلَى الْعَشَاء؟
dialogue.english: Good evening. What will we eat for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ الْخَمِيس، وَغَدًا يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَة.
dialogue.transliteration: al-yawmu yawmu al-khamees, wa ghadan yawmu al-jum3a.
dialogue.english: Today is Thursday, and tomorrow is Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: الْجُمُعَةُ يَوْمُ الصَّلَاةِ وَالرَّاحَة. مَاذَا سَنَفْعَلُ يَوْمَ السَّبْت؟
dialogue.transliteration: al-jum3atu yawmu as-salaati war-raa7a. maadhaa sanaf3alu yawma as-sabt?
dialogue.english: Friday is the day of prayer and rest. What will we do on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Nour
dialogue.arabic: يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ نَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق. تُصْبِحُ عَلَى خَيْر.
dialogue.transliteration: yawma as-sabti nadhhabu ilaa as-sooq. tusbi7u 3alaa khayr.
dialogue.english: On Saturday we go to the market. Good night.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: And you too.
